summary: TAP identifies agents on card-not-present purchases and moves no money, so the rules that bite are card-payment rules: who authorized the transaction (Regulation E and Z, PSD2, UK PSRs), strong customer authentication when the user is absent, and data protection for the IP address, device data and contact values that the consumer object sends to merchants. Visa's rules, which govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law, have since 2025-10-18 made the cardholder responsible, within Visa's system, for an Agentic Payment Provider's actions. Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift, though issuers must pay for Agentic Transactions made under the cardholder's instructions; Worldpay (2026-07-30) says no liability shift exists yet. The Product Terms put consumer disclosures and consents on the implementer. Rows are dated; check each source before relying on it.

rows.text: Card-not-present purchases by a recognized agent fall under Regulation Z for credit cards: unauthorized use means use without actual, implied or apparent authority, with cardholder liability capped at the lesser of $50 or the amount before notice. Whether an agent acting outside its instruction has apparent authority is untested.

For debit cards, Regulation E excludes transfers by a person the consumer gave the access device to, unless the consumer has notified the financial institution that such transfers are no longer authorized. A consumer may therefore carry an agent's transfers until the institution is notified. TAP itself carries no consent record.

TAP adds no sanctions or AML layer. OFAC says compliance obligations are the same whether a transaction is in digital or fiat currency (FAQ 560): U.S. persons must block the property of persons on the SDN List.

California's ADMT regulations took effect on 2026-01-01; a business already using ADMT for significant decisions must comply by 2027-01-01. They cover only significant decisions: providing or denying financial or lending services, housing, education, employment or healthcare. A merchant that uses contextualData or the ID Token only to recognize agents or accept orders is generally not making such a decision.

The RTS on strong customer authentication requires two factors and dynamic linking for remote payments. Visa says every Agentic Ready transaction in Europe used Visa Payment Passkeys to support SCA; that authentication sits in VIC, not in TAP.

PSD2 makes a payment authorized only with the payer's consent and caps payer liability for unauthorized transactions. How consent to a specific transaction applies to an agent instruction is untested; PSD3 and the PSR (provisional agreement 2025-11-27) add no agent rules and are not yet in the Official Journal.

contextualData sends the consumer's IP address, device data, country and postal code to each merchant, and the ID Token carries a stable subject id and obfuscated contact values; under the GDPR these are generally personal data. The TAP Product Terms put disclosures and consents on the implementer.

AI Act Article 50(1) applies from 2026-08-02: providers of AI systems meant to interact directly with people must design them so people know they deal with an AI, unless that is obvious. Generative systems on the market before that date have until 2026-12-02 for the Article 50(2) marking duty. The Digital Omnibus moved Annex III high-risk duties to 2027-12-02; a shopping agent is not high-risk by default.
The Payment Services Regulations 2017 treat a payment as authorized only with the payer's consent (regulation 67) and cap payer liability at GBP 35 in many cases (regulation 77).
HM Treasury's consultation on modernising payment services regulation (2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06) asks how authentication, consent and liability should adapt for agentic payments; no response yet.
The FCA said on 2026-03-25 it will consider with HM Treasury whether regulation must change to support agentic AI payments.

PIPEDA governs the personal information in the consumer object that merchants collect in the course of commercial activities. Collection, use and disclosure within Quebec, Alberta or British Columbia falls under provincial law instead, except at federally regulated businesses (exemption orders under section 26(2)(b)).
No agent-specific payment liability rule was found in Canada; consumer-driven banking phase 2 is targeted for mid-2027.

MAS's E-Payments User Protection Guidelines set liability for unauthorized transactions and duties for erroneous ones on protected accounts. Their liability apportionment does not apply to credit, charge or debit cards issued in Singapore, which follow the ABS Code of Practice for Banks. The Guidelines do not address agents.

MAS issued Guidelines on AI Risk Management on 2026-10-07, effective 2027-10-07, naming agentic AI systems. On 2026-09-10 Ant International, Mastercard and Visa announced they will explore common Know Your Agent principles across their protocols, including TAP. They will work through BuildFin.ai, a MAS-convened platform, building on the SAFR framework (reported).

Visa's rules govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law. Since 2025-10-18 they have required an Agentic Payment Provider to enroll in Visa Intelligent Commerce and register with Visa, directly or via an Agentic Payment Enabler. Within Visa's system, the cardholder is responsible for the provider's actions in an Agentic Transaction as if the cardholder had initiated it, and the provider counts as the Cardholder for that transaction. A merchant must not require a cardholder to waive the right to dispute an Agentic Transaction. The rules do not mention TAP.

Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift and adds no agent-specific dispute condition or fee; its April 2026 US interchange schedule has no agentic category. It does require issuers to pay for Agentic Transactions made under a cardholder's payment instructions and not to block them wholesale. From 2026-10-24 it also accepts an Agentic Payment Provider's login ID among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute. Worldpay wrote on 2026-07-30 that no liability shift exists yet: properly tokenized agent transactions generally follow existing tokenized-transaction rules for fraud, while disputes short of fraud are unsettled.
EMVCo published a draft EMV Agentic Payments framework on 2026-09-01 and lists Know Your Agent and agentic transaction indicators as possible future work; TAP is not an EMVCo document.

A merchant that decrypts the payment payload receives a payment token, expiry and cardholder name, and key-entered checkout handles card numbers; the TAP specification says nothing about PCI DSS scope, while Visa offers Intelligent Commerce Connect to handle PCI compliance for enablers.
